neighbours.label: the verb in a 'get out' idiom meaning news spreading (if the word got out)
fire: If the word got out about the affair, she would resign.
Once the news got out, the phones never stopped.
When word got out that he was ill, crowds came.
The secret got out within a week of the wedding.
If the story gets out, we are all in trouble.
News of the deal got out before the vote.
As soon as the rumor got out, shares fell.
Word got out about the party, and hundreds came.
quiet: If the bus came on time, she would stay.
Once the snow melted, the phones were fixed.
When spring came and he was well, crowds came.
The couple moved within a week of the wedding.
If the rain falls, we are all in the barn.
Copies of the deal were signed before the vote.
As soon as the bell rang, shares fell.
Tickets went on sale for the party, and hundreds came.
